title: Developer Economics Commercialization Playbook
author: Maya Rodriguez
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the product, pricing, rollout, and measurement plan for the Developer Economics initiative: a cohesive set of features and commercial primitives that help self-serve developers understand, control, and convert around inference economics (cost, latency, fidelity). The initiative bundles a lightweight UX in Console + APIs (Consumption Lab), a pricing/costing model (Utility Credits + Fidelity Bands), SDK helpers, and a commercial go-to-market (trial -> conversion ladder).

Intended audience:
- Product managers and PMMs running freemium/PLG funnels
- Developer experience engineers (SDKs, quickstarts)
- Pricing and finance partners
- Sales and solutions engineers supporting mid-market conversions

Goals (high level):
- Reduce time-to-first-meaningful-cost-estimate for new devs to under 10 minutes (measured in sandbox conversion flows).
- Increase trial-to-paid conversion by 18% at cohort level for teams using Consumption Lab within 30 days.
- Reduce average cost-per-query for adoptable workloads by 12% through automated profiling/advisor recommendations.
- Ensure transparent billing that maps fidelity decisions to credit usage with <5% disputes in first 90 days.

Scope (what's included):
- Consumption Lab (Console + API): workload profiler, simulated billing, recommended fidelity profiles.
- Developer Credit Model: Utility Credits + Session Bundles + Fidelity Bands mapping.
- SDK/Quickstarts: cost-aware client helpers, prefetched token heuristics.
- Reporting: per-route cost breakdown, per-tenant fidelity drift alerting.
- Not in scope: enterprise Contract templates, Dedicated reserved capacity billing flows (these stay with sales ops).

Key product components and behaviors:
1) Consumption Lab (Console + API)
   - Inputs: sample prompt set, target latency, target budget per 1k requests.
   - Outputs: predicted credits/month, per-route latency distribution, suggested model variants and quantization profiles.
   - Primary UX: "Profile -> Simulate -> Recommend" flow in Console.

2) Utility Credit Model (pricing primitives)
   - Utility Credit: abstract unit that decouples tokens from bundling for developers. 1 Utility Credit ~= 1k tokens processing for base fidelity on standard models (approx).
   - Fidelity Bands: High / Medium / Low with multiplicative credit factors (High x1.6, Medium x1.0, Low x0.6).
   - Session Bundles: per-minute or per-conversation SKU for conversational workloads (e.g., 100 session-min credit bundle).

3) Cost Advisor (Optimize integration)
   - Automatic recommendations: batching window, prefix caching, model variant selection (fallbacks) with estimated credit delta.
   - API surface: POST /v1/consumption/simulate {promptSet, fidelityTarget, targetBudget} -> simulationId

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Product KPIs:
  - Time to estimate (median): target < 10 minutes
  - Conversion lift: +18% trial->paid for lab users
  - Recommendations adoption rate: > 22% within 14 days
- Financial KPIs:
  - Net new ARR attributable to playbook: $X (tracked in commercial reporting)
  - Dispute rate on invoices from playbook-led contracts: <5% 90-day

Minimum viable requirements (PRD-style checklist):
- [MUST] Consumption Lab prototype with Console flow and public API surface for profiling and simulation.
- [MUST] Fidelity Band definitions and server-side credit multiplier applied to billing pipeline (billing hooks instrumented).
- [MUST] Developer-facing SDK helpers for cost estimation in Node and Python.
- [MUST] Quickstart template repo with sample prompts and CI to run synthetic profiling.
- [SHOULD] Recommendations in Optimize (v2) to feed quantization and batching suggestions.
- [SHOULD] UX for trial credit redemption and conversion prompt.

Configuration table (reference):
| Field | Default | Allowed values | Notes |
|-------|---------|----------------|-------|
| fidelity_band | "medium" | high, medium, low | Maps to credit multiplier in billing pipeline |
| session_bundle_type | "minute" | minute, conversation | Determines session accounting method |
| simulation_horizon_days | "30" | integer days | Used by Consumption Lab for forecast window |

Design constraints and non-functional requirements:
- Data privacy: sample prompts uploaded to Consumption Lab are redacted and only persisted with customer consent; PII detectors required on ingestion.
- Latency: Simulation API must return initial forecast within 8s for typical 50-item prompt sets.
- Accuracy: Predicted credits error target: +/- 12% on 30-day forecast for standard workloads.
- Security: Only authenticated users may run simulations; rate limit to 60 simulations/min per account.

Example API snippet (simulation):
POST /v1/consumption/simulate
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{
  "promptSetId": "sample-ecom-50",
  "fidelityBand": "medium",
  "targetBudgetUsd": 200,
  "horizonDays": 30
}
Response (abridged):
{
  "simulationId": "sim-20270713-001",
  "predictedCredits": 3200,
  "predictedCostUsd": 192.00,
  "recommendations": ["medium-quantize-8bit", "batch-window-16"]
}

Rollout plan (phased):
1. Alpha (4 weeks): internal teams + 5 pilot customers. Deliverables: Consumption Lab alpha UX, Node SDK cost estimator, billing multiplier proof-of-concept.
2. Private Beta (8 weeks): 25 customers across SMB and mid-market. Deliverables: Console UX polish, Python SDK, billing hooks in sandbox, Optimize recommendations wired.
3. General Availability (GA, 12 weeks): public release, GA docs, pricing page updates, marketing collateral. Deliverables: full billing integration, trial credit flows, commercial playbook for sales.

Rollout checklist (owners):
- Product PM: Maya Rodriguez (owner)
- Engineering: Diego Alvarez (consumption API), SRE: Hannah Li (rate limits, infra), SDK: Priya Singh (Node/Python)
- Pricing & Finance: Olivia Park (credit conversion rules), Legal: Ben Carter (terms for trial credit)
- Marketing/PMM: Liam Chen (launch assets)

Pricing and packaging guidance (commercial):
- Trial: 1,000 Utility Credits for new dev signups for 30 days. Automatic expiration, non-transferable.
- Conversion path: customers who run a simulation and hit predictedCostUsd > $150 within 14 days are eligible for a 15% first-year credit on committed plans.
- Price tiers (illustrative):
  - Developer (self-serve): pay-as-you-go utility credits, fidelity multipliers apply.
  - Team: discounted session-bundles with 10% committed discount.
  - Enterprise: custom contract; Dedicated billing flows remain separate and handled by Sales Ops.

Billing reconciliation notes:
- Billing pipeline will multiply base token consumption by fidelity multiplier before mapping to Utility Credits. Reconciliation exports must include: simulationId (if used), fidelityBand, appliedMultiplier, and related route id.
- Finance must be able to flag invoices that differ from simulations by >20% for manual review.

Release notes (initial GA):
- Consumption Lab: Profile -> Simulate -> Recommend flow in Console and Simulation API.
- Pricing primitives: Fidelity Bands and Utility Credit mechanics live in billing sandbox.
- SDKs: Node and Python cost estimator v0.9.
- Known limitations: simulation accuracy degrades for heavy multimodal workloads; session bundles for multimodal are beta.

Measurement and experimentation plan:
- A/B experiment: surface Consumption Lab to 50% of new signups; primary metric: trial->paid conversion at 30 days. Secondary: time-to-first-estimate.
- Funnel instrumentation: track "ran_simulation", "accepted_recommendation", "purchased_commitment" events with attribution to simulationId.
- Data exports: weekly cohort reports and finance reconciliation.

Open decisions (action items):
- D1: Finalize Utility Credit to USD conversion factor for public pricing page (owner: Olivia Park) — due 2027-07-20.
- D2: Decide whether session bundles should be meter-based (minutes) or event-based (conversations) for conversational-first customers (owner: PM + Sales).
- D3: Define grace policy for simulation discrepancies >30% and automated crediting (owner: Finance/Legal).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customers see discrepancy between simulation and billed amounts -> Mitigation: conservative simulation defaults, explicit "error band" in UI, and dispute workflow linking to reconciliation exports.
- Risk: Complexity of fidelity multipliers confuses developers -> Mitigation: clear default presets, simple "economy"/"balanced"/"quality" quick toggles, sample cost examples in quickstart.

Next steps (2-week):
1. Engineering scoping session to estimate integration points with billing pipeline (owners: Diego, Olivia)
2. UX wireframes for Consumption Lab Console (owner: Liam Chen)
3. Establish simulation QA harness and accuracy targets with Applied ML (owner: Priya Singh)

Appendix: example quickstart README excerpt
- Step 1: clone repo and set REDWOOD_API_KEY
- Step 2: run npm run profile --sample=sample-ecom-50
- Step 3: POST results to /v1/consumption/simulate to receive recommendations

Frequently asked questions:
Q: Will consumption simulations ever be billable?
A: Simulations themselves are free within trial limits. Running large-scale production simulations ( >10,000 prompts) may be rate-limited and require sandbox credits.

Q: How do fidelity bands interact with model fallback?
A: Recommendations include compatible fallback variants. Billing applies the highest fidelity multiplier that was actually served; we log variant decisions for reconciliation.
